repo.name: native
repo.description: Dart packages related to native interop and the foreign function interface. Contains code generators for generating bindings for other programming languages and packages related to the hooks system for bundling native code,

issue.title: [objective_c] support `scheduleInRunLoop:forMode:`
issue.body_html:
Description

The NSInputStream returned by toNSInputStream currently ignores scheduleInRunLoop:forMode:.

This causes NSURLSession to make read:maxLength calls on its single, process-wide com.apple.NSURLConnectionLoader thread, which waits until the Dart stream provides data. This really hurts package:cupertino_http's performance when performing concurrent uploads.

Related Issues

Fixes #3750
Fixes #3752

PR Checklist

  • I’ve reviewed the contributor guide and applied the relevant portions to this PR.
  • I've run dart tool/ci.dart --all locally and resolved all issues identified. This ensures the PR is formatted, has no lint errors, and ran all code generators. This applies to the packages part of the toplevel pubspec.yaml workspace.
  • All existing and new tests are passing. I added new tests to check the change I am making.
  • The PR is actually solving the issue. PRs that don't solve the issue will be closed. Please be respectful of the maintainers' time. If it's not clear what the issue is, feel free to ask questions on the GitHub issue before submitting a PR.
  • I have updated CHANGELOG.md for the relevant packages. (Not needed for small changes such as doc typos).
  • I have updated the pubspec package version if necessary.

issue.body:
## Description

The `NSInputStream` returned by `toNSInputStream` currently ignores [`scheduleInRunLoop:forMode:`](https://github.com/dart-lang/native/blob/3cbe319e3c1ec0f9253c126ba3e465e55229c3a4/pkgs/objective_c/src/input_stream_adapter.m#L66-L67).

This causes `NSURLSession` to make [read:maxLength](https://github.com/dart-lang/native/blob/3cbe319e3c1ec0f9253c126ba3e465e55229c3a4/pkgs/objective_c/src/input_stream_adapter.m#L131) calls on its single, process-wide `com.apple.NSURLConnectionLoader thread`, which [waits](https://github.com/dart-lang/native/blob/3cbe319e3c1ec0f9253c126ba3e465e55229c3a4/pkgs/objective_c/src/input_stream_adapter.m#L163) until the Dart stream provides data. This really hurts `package:cupertino_http`'s performance when performing concurrent uploads.

## Related Issues

Fixes #3750
Fixes #3752 

## PR Checklist

- [X] I’ve reviewed the [contributor guide](https://github.com/dart-lang/native/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and applied the relevant portions to this PR.
- [X] I've run `dart tool/ci.dart --all` locally and resolved all issues identified. This ensures the PR is formatted, has no lint errors, and ran all code generators. This applies to the packages part of the toplevel `pubspec.yaml` workspace.
- [X] All existing and new tests are passing. I added new tests to check the change I am making.
- [X] The PR is actually solving the issue. PRs that don't solve the issue will be closed. Please be respectful of the maintainers' time. If it's not clear what the issue is, feel free to ask questions on the GitHub issue before submitting a PR.
- [X] I have updated `CHANGELOG.md` for the relevant packages. (Not needed for small changes such as doc typos).
- [X] I have [updated the pubspec package version](https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/blob/main/docs/External-Package-Maintenance.md#making-a-change) if necessary.

Codecov provides highly integrated tools to group, merge, archive and compare coverage reports. Whether your team is comparing changes in a pull request or reviewing a single commit, Codecov will improve the code review workflow and quality.

## Code coverage done right.®

1. Upload coverage reports from your CI builds.
2. Codecov merges all builds and languages into one beautiful coherent report.
3. Get commit statuses, pull request comments and coverage overlay via our browser extension.

When Codecov merges your uploads it keeps track of the CI provider (inc. build details) and user specified context, e.g. `#unittest` ~ `#smoketest` or `#oldcode` ~ `#newcode`. You can track the `#unittest` coverage independently of other groups. [Learn more here](
http://docs.codecov.io/docs/flags)

Through **Codecov's Browser Extension** reports overlay directly in GitHub UI to assist in code review in [Chrome](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/codecov/gedikamndpbemklijjkncpnolildpbgo) or Firefox (https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/codecov/)

*Highly detailed* **pull request comments** and *customizable* **commit statuses** will improve your team's workflow and code coverage incrementally.

**File backed configuration** all through the `codecov.yml`. 

## FAQ
- Do you **merge multiple uploads** to the same commit? **Yes**
- Do you **support multiple languages** in the same project? **Yes**
- Can you **group coverage reports** by project and/or test type? **Yes**
- How does **pricing** work? Only paid users can view reports and post statuses/comments.

pull.title: [objective_c] support `scheduleInRunLoop:forMode:`
pull.body:
## Description

The `NSInputStream` returned by `toNSInputStream` currently ignores [`scheduleInRunLoop:forMode:`](https://github.com/dart-lang/native/blob/3cbe319e3c1ec0f9253c126ba3e465e55229c3a4/pkgs/objective_c/src/input_stream_adapter.m#L66-L67).

This causes `NSURLSession` to make [read:maxLength](https://github.com/dart-lang/native/blob/3cbe319e3c1ec0f9253c126ba3e465e55229c3a4/pkgs/objective_c/src/input_stream_adapter.m#L131) calls on its single, process-wide `com.apple.NSURLConnectionLoader thread`, which [waits](https://github.com/dart-lang/native/blob/3cbe319e3c1ec0f9253c126ba3e465e55229c3a4/pkgs/objective_c/src/input_stream_adapter.m#L163) until the Dart stream provides data. This really hurts `package:cupertino_http`'s performance when performing concurrent uploads.

## Related Issues

Fixes #3750
Fixes #3752

issue.title: [objective_c] `NSInputStream` can deadlock

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Needs triage from the team. Remove this label once triaged.

issue.body_html:
The NSInputStream returned by toNSInputStream will deadlock if native code calls read:maxLength and the Dart isolate backing it exits before providing any data.

CFNetwork does these reads on its single, process-wide com.apple.NSURLConnectionLoader thread. When it hangs, every NSURLSession request in the process stops, and cancelling tasks can't finish.

The exact code location of the lock being held that will never be released.

To reproduce, add this to pkgs/objective_c/test/ns_input_stream_test.dart:

test('isolate exit while read is blocked', () async {
  final ready = ReceivePort();
  await Isolate.spawn((SendPort sendPort) async {
    final controller = StreamController<List<int>>();
    final stream = controller.stream.toNSInputStream();
    final exitPort = ReceivePort();
    sendPort.send((stream, exitPort.sendPort));
    await exitPort.first;
    Isolate.exit();
  }, ready.sendPort);

  final (isolatedStream, exitSendPort) =
      await ready.first as (NSInputStream, SendPort);
  isolatedStream.open();
  final readFuture = read(isolatedStream, 10);
  await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 100));
  exitSendPort.send(null);
  final (count, data, hasBytesAvailable, status, error) =
      await readFuture;
  expect(count, -1);
  expect(data, isEmpty);
  expect(hasBytesAvailable, false);
  expect(status, NSStreamStatus.NSStreamStatusError);
  expect(error, isNotNull);
  isolatedStream.close();
});

issue.title: [objective_c] `NSInputStream` doesn't support run loop scheduling

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Needs triage from the team. Remove this label once triaged.

issue.body_html:
The NSInputStream returned by toNSInputStream ignores scheduleInRunLoop:forMode:, never sends stream events to its delegate, and hasBytesAvailable returns YES even when no data is buffered. So a reader that schedules the stream and waits for events never receives any.

NSURLSession schedules request body streams, but because hasBytesAvailable returns YES, it calls read:maxLength on its single, process-wide com.apple.NSURLConnectionLoader thread, which waits until the Dart stream provides data. Until then, no other NSURLSession request in the process can make progress. package:cupertino_http sends StreamedRequest bodies this way.

To reproduce, add this to pkgs/objective_c/test/ns_input_stream_test.dart:

test('hasBytesAvailable when scheduled in a run loop', () {
  final controller = StreamController<List<int>>();
  final inputStream = controller.stream.toNSInputStream();
  addTearDown(inputStream.close);
  inputStream.scheduleInRunLoop(
    NSRunLoop.getCurrentRunLoop(),
    forMode: 'kCFRunLoopDefaultMode'.toNSString(),
  );
  inputStream.open();
  expect(inputStream.hasBytesAvailable, isFalse);
});
